slides.title: Browser vs Node.js
slides.html:
Node.js

Browser vs Node.js

Browser

window, document, DOM, clicks. Can't read your files.

document.querySelector()

Node.js

No DOM. Files, network, processes, servers.

fs.readFile()

Both

Same JavaScript: variables, functions, arrays, async.

const, map, await

slides.title: Running JavaScript with Node
slides.html:
Run

Running JavaScript with Node

  • Check your version: node -v
  • Run a file: node app.js
  • node --watch reruns on save
  • Type node alone for a REPL

Terminal

// app.js
const name = "BlockHub";
console.log(`Hello from ${name}!`);
console.log(process.version);
 
$ node app.js
Hello from BlockHub!
v22.11.0
 
$ node --watch app.js

slides.title: Modules: split code into files
slides.html:
Modules

Modules: split code into files

math.js

// math.js
export const add = (a, b) => a + b;
export const PI = 3.14;
 
export default function square(n) {
  return n * n;
}

app.js

// app.js
import square, { add, PI } from "./math.js";
 
console.log(add(2, 3));  // 5
console.log(square(4));  // 16

Add "type": "module" to package.json

slides.title: npm and package.json
slides.html:
npm

npm and package.json

  • npm init -y creates package.json
  • dependencies: needed to run
  • devDependencies: only for development
  • scripts: shortcuts you run with npm run

package.json

npm init -y
npm install chalk
npm install -D nodemon
 
{
  "name": "notes-cli",
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": { "start": "node index.js" },
  "dependencies": { "chalk": "^5.3.0" },
  "devDependencies": { "nodemon": "^3.1.0" }
}

slides.title: Reading and writing files
slides.html:
Files

Reading and writing files

  • Use the promises version of fs
  • Always say "utf8" for text
  • Wrap in try/catch: files can be missing

files.js

import fs from "node:fs/promises";
 
await fs.writeFile("hello.txt", "Hi there\n");
await fs.appendFile("hello.txt", "Another line\n");
 
const text = await fs.readFile("hello.txt", "utf8");
console.log(text);
 
const files = await fs.readdir(".");
await fs.unlink("hello.txt"); // delete

slides.title: path and process
slides.html:
Paths

path and process

  • path.join builds paths that work on every OS
  • import.meta.dirname: this file's folder
  • process.env: environment variables
  • process.exit(1): stop with an error

paths.js

import path from "node:path";
 
const file = path.join(import.meta.dirname, "data", "notes.json");
path.extname(file);   // ".json"
path.basename(file);  // "notes.json"
 
process.env.NODE_ENV  // "development"
process.cwd()         // where you ran node from
process.exit(1)

slides.title: The event loop
slides.html:
Event loop

The event loop

  • Node runs your code on one thread
  • Slow work (files, network) runs in the background
  • When it's done, its callback joins the queue
  • So Node never sits waiting

Order of output

console.log("1. start");
 
setTimeout(() => console.log("3. timer"), 0);
 
fs.readFile("big.txt", "utf8").then(() =>
  console.log("4. file read"));
 
console.log("2. end");
 
// 1. start 2. end 3. timer 4. file read

slides.title: Callbacks → Promises → async/await
slides.html:
Async

Callbacks → Promises → async/await

  • Callbacks nest and get messy
  • Promises chain with .then
  • async/await reads top to bottom
  • Use try/catch for errors

Three styles

// callback
fs.readFile("a.txt", "utf8", (err, data) => { /* ... */ });
 
// promise
fsp.readFile("a.txt", "utf8").then(console.log).catch(console.error);
 
// async/await
try {
  const data = await fsp.readFile("a.txt", "utf8");
} catch (err) {
  console.error("Could not read file:", err.message);
}

slides.title: Command-line arguments
slides.html:
CLI

Command-line arguments

  • process.argv holds what was typed
  • The first two are node and the file
  • Your arguments start at index 2

notes.js

// node notes.js add "Buy milk"
const [, , command, ...rest] = process.argv;
 
command          // "add"
rest.join(" ")   // "Buy milk"
 
if (!command) {
  console.log("Usage: node notes.js <add|list|remove> [text]");
  process.exit(1);
}

slides.title: Saving notes to a file
slides.html:
Build

Saving notes to a file

  • Load returns [] if the file is missing
  • Save writes pretty JSON
  • Every command: load → change → save

storage.js

import fs from "node:fs/promises";
const FILE = "notes.json";
 
export async function load() {
  try {
    return JSON.parse(await fs.readFile(FILE, "utf8"));
  } catch {
    return [];
  }
}
 
export const save = (notes) =>
  fs.writeFile(FILE, JSON.stringify(notes, null, 2));

slides.title: Handling commands
slides.html:
Build

Handling commands

  • Read the command from process.argv
  • Change the array
  • Save and print a message

index.js

const notes = await load();
 
if (command === "add") {
  notes.push({ id: Date.now(), text: rest.join(" ") });
  await save(notes);
  console.log("Note added ✅");
} else if (command === "list") {
  notes.forEach((n, i) => console.log(`${i + 1}. ${n.text}`));
} else {
  console.log("Unknown command:", command);
}
